title.value: Counting laminae against the 2258 core boxes at Beacon House

description.value: Two days in the beacon hut with an old core box and a fresh core from the same station. The laminae match to the year, again.

content.value:
Two days in the beacon hut with the third core box from 2258 and a fresh core taken at the same station in October. Counting was done twice by two people separately and then once together.

The laminae match across the whole overlap. Forty-seven years between the marker laminae, forty-seven years on the log. It remains the only clock in this half of the galaxy and it has still never been wrong.

Three laminae from the 2270s run at about a third of the usual thickness. There is no ice record for those years and nothing else on the transect to check them against, so we can say the mat had a poor decade and nothing whatever about why.

Otherwise nothing happened. The beacon was running when we arrived and was running when we left. The visitors' log held fourteen entries, the earliest 2258 and the latest 2298, and now holds fifteen.

fieldConditions: Ice, no weather, and the hut warmer than the shelter we did not deploy. Two of us for the whole of it and nobody within four hundred kilometres.

notes.value: The core boxes stay at Beacon House. Shipping them costs more than re-coring, and the hut is colder than any store the sector could build.
